title: Ordinary Kunneth at a finite coefficient ring
statement:
Let $k$ be the algebraically closed field of
[def-weil-finite-field-fiber], and let $X,Y$ be
separated finite-type
$k$-schemes. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, for $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $n\geq1$, and $\ell\neq\operatorname{char}(k)$.
Use the ordinary unbounded small etale derived categories of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], the derived tensor of [def-kun-derived-tensor], and the canonical Kunneth arrow of [def-kun-kunneth-map].
For $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and
$L\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ in the
derived categories,
write $K\boxtimes_A^L L=p_X^*K\otimes_A^Lp_Y^*L$, using the
derived tensor product.
The exterior-product map is an isomorphism

$$
R\Gamma(X,K)\otimes_A^LR\Gamma(Y,L)
\longrightarrow R\Gamma(X\times_kY,K\boxtimes_A^L L).
$$

proof.text: Fix the coefficient data of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Thus $\mathcal O_E$ is a DVR, $A$ is finite, and $\kappa=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E)=A/(\varpi_E)$ is a finite field. Its characteristic is $\ell$: the extended absolute value has $|\ell|_E=\ell^{-1}<1$, so $\ell\in(\varpi_E)$. In particular $A$ is a torsion ring. The schemes $X,Y,Z=X\times_kY$ are qcqs and finite type over the separably closed field $k$. For the product, on finite affine covers its coordinate algebras are $B_i\otimes_k C_j$, generated by the generators of $B_i$ and $C_j$; The diagonal of $Z$ is the product of the two closed diagonals (after permuting the factors), so [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-products] makes it a closed immersion. Apply [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated] to the three structure morphisms. Over the affine base $\operatorname{Spec}k$, this gives quasi-separated sources: for affine opens $U,V$, their intersection is the inverse image of the affine open $U\times_kV$ under the quasi-compact relative diagonal and is quasi-compact. These observations check all geometric and coefficient hypotheses used below.

We will use coefficient restriction without changing derived sections. For any ring map $R\to S$ and scheme $T$, restriction of scalars is exact and conservative: kernels, cokernels and cohomology have the same underlying abelian sheaves. Its derived functor is therefore termwise restriction. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to the two factorizations of the ringed-topos morphism $(T_{\mathrm{et}},S_T)\to(*,R)$, through $(T_{\mathrm{et}},R_T)$ and through $(*,S)$. Their equality gives the canonical natural isomorphism
$$R\Gamma_R(T,\operatorname{Res}H)\cong\operatorname{Res}R\Gamma_S(T,H).$$
The resolution normalization in that node identifies this with the comparison induced by the identity of underlying section complexes. Thus it respects coefficient endomorphisms. A termwise splitting $M=eM\oplus(1-e)M$ remains a splitting under $R\Gamma$: finite sums of K-injective complexes are K-injective, since Hom into their sum is the finite sum of the acyclic Hom complexes. Consequently $R\Gamma(eM)=eR\Gamma(M)$. No claim that restriction preserves K-injectivity is needed.

proof.text: First let $B$ be any finite field of characteristic $\ell$ and let $P\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},B)$, $Q\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},B)$. Apply [thm-kun-0f1p] with $n=\ell$ to their restrictions to $F=\mathbf F_\ell$. Its arrow is $B\otimes_F B$-linear: naturality for multiplication on $P$ and on $Q$ gives the two commuting actions. Apply the diagonal projector of [lem-pur-finite-field-derived-tensor-summand] to this isomorphism. On the source its image is $\operatorname{Res}(R\Gamma_B(X,P)\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}R\Gamma_B(Y,Q))$ by that lemma and step 2. On the target it is $\operatorname{Res}R\Gamma_B(Z,p_X^{-1}P\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}p_Y^{-1}Q)$, using the same lemma on $Z$ and step 2. These identifications give the $B$-Kunneth arrow itself: under [def-kun-kunneth-map] its adjunct is the tensor of the two counits; the balanced tensor quotient sends the $F$-linear adjunct to the $B$-linear adjunct. Restriction is conservative by step 2, so this arrow is an isomorphism for arbitrary unbounded $P,Q$.

By [lem-kun-0f10] each of $X,Y,Z$ has finite cohomological dimension. For $H\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ put $H_\kappa=H\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}\kappa_T$ as an object of $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},\kappa)$ using [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Construct the canonical scalar comparison as a morphism in $D(\kappa)$:
$$c_{T,H}:R\Gamma_A(T,H)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}\kappa\longrightarrow R\Gamma_\kappa(T,H_\kappa).$$
Precisely, its adjunct under constant $\kappa$-complex versus derived sections is the scalar extension of the $A$-counit $\underline{R\Gamma_A(T,H)}\to H$. The identification of its pulled-back source with the scalar extension of that constant complex is the pullback-tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Under step 2, the restriction of this morphism to $D(A)$ is the constant-tensor comparison [def-kun-projection-formula-map]: both adjuncts are the same $A$-counit tensor $1_\kappa$. Apply [lem-kun-0f12] at the torsion ring $A$ with the coefficient complex $\kappa[0]$ to conclude that this underlying comparison is an isomorphism. Since restriction is conservative, $c_{T,H}$ is an isomorphism in $D(\kappa)$. This constructs the $\kappa$-linear morphism itself; no lifting of an arbitrary $A$-derived morphism from a commuting coefficient action is asserted.

Write $S_T=-\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}\kappa_T$ and $S_*=-\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}\kappa$. The monoidal scalar-extension isomorphism in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], applied to the identity topos with ring map $A_T\to\kappa_T$, identifies $S_T(H\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}J)$ with $S_TH\otimes_\kappa^{\mathbf L}S_TJ$; the same applies on the point site. Inverse image commutes with this coefficient extension by [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] applied over $A$ with the second factor $\underline\kappa$. Hence, with $a_A$ the item’s arrow and $a_\kappa$ the arrow for $K_\kappa,L_\kappa$, the comparisons of step 4 give the square
$$c_{Z,K\boxtimes_A^LL}\circ S_*(a_A)=a_\kappa\circ(c_{X,K}\otimes_\kappa^{\mathbf L}c_{Y,L}),$$
where the target is identified with $R\Gamma_\kappa(Z,K_\kappa\boxtimes_\kappa^LL_\kappa)$ by the preceding tensor isomorphisms. To check this equality, use [def-kun-projection-formula-map] to expand each $c$ as the adjunct of counit tensor identity and [def-kun-kunneth-map] to expand $a$ as the adjunct of the two counits. Pull both composites back to $Z$ and take their adjuncts. After the canonical tensor rebracketing both are
$$(p_X^{-1}\varepsilon_X\otimes p_Y^{-1}\varepsilon_Y)\otimes1_{\kappa_Z},$$
from $p_X^{-1}\underline{R\Gamma_A(X,K)}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}p_Y^{-1}\underline{R\Gamma_A(Y,L)}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}\kappa_Z$ to $K\boxtimes_A^LL\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}\kappa_Z$. Here $\varepsilon_X:\underline{R\Gamma_A(X,K)}\to K$ and $\varepsilon_Y:\underline{R\Gamma_A(Y,L)}\to L$ are the counits for constant sheaf versus global sections, and the pullbacks of the constant complexes to $Z$ are identified. Equality of adjuncts proves the square. Thus this is an equality of the canonical maps, not merely an isomorphism of their endpoints.

Step 3 with $B=\kappa$ proves that $a_\kappa$ is an isomorphism; its arguments $K_\kappa,L_\kappa$ need not be bounded. Step 4 and the square in step 5 imply that $S_*(a_A)$ is an isomorphism. Let $D$ be a cone of $a_A$ in $D(A)$. By the exactness of derived scalar extension in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], its reduction is a cone of $S_*(a_A)$, hence $D\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}\kappa=0$.

Put $I_i=\varpi_E^iA$ for $0\leq i\leq n$, so $I_0=A$, $I_n=0$. For $i<n$, multiplication by $\varpi_E^i$ identifies $\kappa$ with $I_i/I_{i+1}$ as $A$-modules: it is surjective, and if $\varpi_E^iu\in\varpi_E^{i+1}\mathcal O_E$ then cancellation in the DVR gives $u\in\varpi_E\mathcal O_E$. Choose a K-flat resolution $P$ of $D$ with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on the one-point site. For any $A$-module $M$, $P\otimes_A M$ computes $D\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M$: choose a K-flat resolution $Q\to M$, use [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] for $P\otimes_AQ$, and use the K-flat condition [def-pc-kflat-complex] to see that $P\otimes_A\operatorname{Cone}(Q\to M)$ is acyclic. Flatness of every $P^r$ makes $0\to P\otimes_AI_{i+1}\to P\otimes_AI_i\to P\otimes_A\kappa\to0$ a degreewise exact sequence of complexes. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] this is a distinguished triangle after localization. Downward induction starts with $P\otimes_AI_n=0$; if $P\otimes_AI_{i+1}$ is acyclic, its triangle and step 6 imply $P\otimes_AI_i$ is acyclic. At $i=0$, $P\otimes_AA\cong P$ by the chain isomorphism $p\otimes a\mapsto ap$, with inverse $p\mapsto p\otimes1$. Hence $D=0$ and $a_A$ is an isomorphism. This proves the stated canonical arrow without any boundedness assumption.
